title: Range of a Bounded Rational Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the range of f(x)=1/(x^2+1) over all real x.

steps.title: Bound the Denominator
steps.explanation: Since x^2 ranges over [0, infinity), adding 1 makes the denominator sweep out [1, infinity).
steps.why: Squares are nonnegative, and equality occurs at x=0.

steps.title: Invert the Inequality
steps.explanation: Taking reciprocals of positive quantities reverses the order, so the outputs lie between 0 (exclusive) and 1 (inclusive).
steps.why: For 0 < a <= b one has 1/b <= 1/a, and a positive numerator keeps the fraction positive.

steps.title: Check Endpoint Attainment
steps.explanation: The maximum 1 occurs at x=0, while the value 0 is only a limiting value as |x| grows, never an actual output.
steps.why: Range endpoints count only when some finite input produces them.

steps.title: Conclude the Range
steps.explanation: Continuity fills every intermediate value, so the outputs are exactly the positives up to and including 1.
steps.why: The function is continuous, attains 1, and remains strictly between 0 and 1 elsewhere.
